regen_doc:
AWS Lake Formation integrates with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) so that you can more easily set up other integrated services to encrypt and decrypt data in Amazon S3 locations. Both customer managed keys and AWS managed keys are supported, but client-side encryption/decryption is not.

You should avoid registering an Amazon S3 bucket that has Requester pays enabled. For buckets registered with Lake Formation, the role used to register the bucket is always viewed as the requester. If the bucket is accessed by another AWS account, the bucket owner is charged for data access if the role belongs to the same account as the bucket owner.

To register an AWS KMS-encrypted Amazon S3 bucket in account B using an IAM role in account A, two conditions must be met: the role in account A must grant permissions on the bucket in account B, and the bucket policy in account B must grant access permissions to the role in account A. If the KMS key is in account B, the key policy must also grant access to the role in account A, and the role in account A must grant permissions on the KMS key. Lake Formation assumes the registered role when accessing underlying data in Amazon S3, and that assumed role has the required permissions on the KMS key. As a result, you don't have to grant permissions on the KMS key to principals accessing underlying data with ETL jobs or with integrated services such as Amazon Athena.

You can't use the Lake Formation service-linked role to register a location in another account. Instead, you must use a user-defined role that meets the requirements in Requirements for roles used to register locations. The role used for registration is created in the AWS account that contains the Data Catalog (account A), and it must include a policy that grants Amazon S3 permissions on the location. If the KMS key is not in the same account as the Data Catalog, an inline policy granting the required permissions on the KMS key must be added to the role.

The bucket policy on the Amazon S3 console must grant the role the required S3 permissions: s3:ListBucket on the bucket, and s3:DeleteObject, s3:GetObject, and s3:PutObject on the objects. In AWS KMS, the role's ARN must be added to the Allow use of the key object in the key policy of the KMS key. If that object is missing from the key policy, you add it with the permissions shown in the example.

Registration in Lake Formation is done by signing in to the Data Catalog AWS account as the data lake administrator. Because cross-account buckets do not appear in the list when you choose Browse, you must type the S3 path. On the Register location page, you choose the role as the IAM role and then choose Register location.

regen_doc:
## Encrypting and registering Amazon S3 locations with AWS Lake Formation

AWS Lake Formation integrates with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) so that you can more easily set up other integrated services to encrypt and decrypt data in Amazon S3 locations. Both customer managed keys and AWS managed keys are supported. Client-side encryption/decryption is not supported.

You should avoid registering an Amazon S3 bucket that has Requester pays enabled. For buckets registered with Lake Formation, the role used to register the bucket is always viewed as the requester. If the bucket is accessed by another AWS account, the bucket owner is charged for data access if the role belongs to the same account as the bucket owner.

### Cross-account registration of AWS KMS-encrypted buckets

Registering an AWS KMS-encrypted Amazon S3 bucket in account B using an IAM role in account A requires two things: the role in account A must grant permissions on the bucket in account B, and the bucket policy in account B must grant access permissions to the role in account A. If the KMS key is in account B, the key policy must grant access to the role in account A, and the role in account A must grant permissions on the KMS key.

Lake Formation assumes the registered role when accessing underlying data in Amazon S3, and the assumed role has the required permissions on the KMS key. As a result, you don't have to grant permissions on the KMS key to principals accessing underlying data with ETL jobs or with integrated services such as Amazon Athena.

You can't use the Lake Formation service-linked role to register a location in another account. To register a location in another account, you must use a user-defined role that meets the requirements in Requirements for roles used to register locations.

### Role and policy requirements

The role used for registration is created in the AWS account that contains the Data Catalog (account A). The role must include a policy that grants Amazon S3 permissions on the location. If the KMS key is not in the same account as the Data Catalog, an inline policy granting the required permissions on the KMS key must be added to the role.

The bucket policy on the Amazon S3 console must grant the role the required S3 permissions: s3:ListBucket on the bucket, and s3:DeleteObject, s3:GetObject, and s3:PutObject on the objects.

In AWS KMS, the role's ARN must be added to the Allow use of the key object in the key policy of the KMS key. If the Allow use of the key object is missing from the key policy, you add it with the permissions shown in the example.

### Registering the location

Registration in Lake Formation is done by signing in to the Data Catalog AWS account as the data lake administrator. Because cross-account buckets do not appear in the list when you choose Browse, you must type the S3 path. On the Register location page, you choose the role as the IAM role and then choose Register location.

# Registering a cross-account, AWS KMS-encrypted Amazon S3 location

## Before you begin

Make sure you have the following in place before you start:

- An existing KMS key (customer managed or AWS managed) that encrypts the data in the S3 bucket.
- A user-defined IAM role in the Data Catalog account (account A) that meets the registration role requirements and includes a policy granting Amazon S3 permissions on the location. The Lake Formation service-linked role cannot be used. Steps: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/registration-role.html
- An IAM policy on that role granting Amazon S3 permissions on the bucket location in account B.
- An inline IAM policy on the role granting the required permissions on the KMS key, needed when the KMS key is in a different account than the Data Catalog. Steps are on this page.
- A bucket policy in account B granting the account A role the required S3 permissions. Steps are on this page.
- A KMS key policy allowing the account A role to use the KMS key that encrypts the location. Steps are on this page.
- Data lake administrator access to the Lake Formation console in the Data Catalog account.

## Encryption support and bucket considerations

AWS Lake Formation integrates with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) so that you can more easily set up other integrated services to encrypt and decrypt data in Amazon S3 locations. Both customer managed keys and AWS managed keys are supported. Client-side encryption/decryption is not supported.

You should avoid registering an Amazon S3 bucket that has Requester pays enabled. For buckets registered with Lake Formation, the role used to register the bucket is always viewed as the requester. If the bucket is accessed by another AWS account, the bucket owner is charged for data access if the role belongs to the same account as the bucket owner.

## Cross-account requirements

Registering an AWS KMS-encrypted Amazon S3 bucket in account B using an IAM role in account A requires two things: the role in account A must grant permissions on the bucket in account B, and the bucket policy in account B must grant access permissions to the role in account A. Only when both hold can you use a user-defined role to register a location in another account. You can't use the Lake Formation service-linked role to register a location in another account. You must use a user-defined role that meets the requirements in Requirements for roles used to register locations.

If the KMS key is in account B, the key policy must grant access to the role in account A, and the role in account A must grant permissions on the KMS key.

Lake Formation assumes the registered role when accessing underlying data in Amazon S3, and the assumed role has the required permissions on the KMS key. Together, these are enough that you don't have to grant permissions on the KMS key to principals accessing underlying data with ETL jobs or with integrated services such as Amazon Athena.

## Set up the role and policies

The role used for registration is created in the AWS account that contains the Data Catalog (account A). The role must include a policy that grants Amazon S3 permissions on the location. If the KMS key is not in the same account as the Data Catalog, an inline policy granting the required permissions on the KMS key must be added to the role.

On the Amazon S3 console, the bucket policy must grant the role the required S3 permissions: s3:ListBucket on the bucket, and s3:DeleteObject, s3:GetObject, and s3:PutObject on the objects.

In AWS KMS, the role's ARN must be added to the Allow use of the key object in the key policy of the KMS key. If the Allow use of the key object is missing from the key policy, you add it with the permissions shown in the example.

## Register the location

Complete the role policy, the bucket policy, and the KMS key policy changes above before you register; all three must be in place before the final registration step.

Registration in Lake Formation is done by signing in to the Data Catalog AWS account as the data lake administrator. You must type the S3 path because cross-account buckets do not appear in the list when you choose Browse. Typing the path is enough to proceed. On the Register location page, you choose the role as the IAM role and then choose Register location.
